**Red flags for suspicious messages:**
- Unsolicited "urgent" medical advice from unknown sources
- Claims of being from prestigious institutions without verifiable contact info
- Pressure to act immediately without consulting your own healthcare providers
- Requests for personal medical information
- Promotion of "miracle cures" or treatments that sound too good to be true

**Warning signs of unreliable medical information:**
- Dramatic claims like "doctors don't want you to know this"
- Anecdotal evidence presented as scientific proof
- Advice to stop prescribed medications without medical supervision
- No author credentials or sources cited
- Information that contradicts established medical consensus without peer-reviewed evidence
- Promotion of expensive supplements or treatments

**For your wellness center's social media, consider:**
- Only sharing information from established health organizations (CDC, NIH, Mayo Clinic, etc.)
- Always including disclaimers that information isn't a substitute for professional medical advice
- Encouraging people to discuss any health information with their healthcare providers
- Being extra cautious with anything related to medications, treatments, or diagnoses

**Helpful resources for medication safety education:**
- FDA's "Your Guide to Safe Use of Medicine" materials
- AARP's medication management resources
- National Institute on Aging's medication safety guides
- Local pharmacy chains often have free educational materials

The idea about having a healthcare professional on our advisory board is brilliant - I wonder if one of the local doctors or nurses who sometimes volunteer with us would be interested in that role.

You've been incredibly helpful and patient with all my questions. I feel so much more confident now about how to handle health information responsibly. It's reassuring to know there are people like you who really understand these issues and can help guide folks like me who are trying to do the right thing.

I should probably get going - I want to start looking into those FDA and AARP resources while I still have some time today. But seriously, thank you again for taking the time to walk me through all of this. You've probably helped me avoid some real mistakes down the road!

<END>
